subject: Lighting and power for productive work
hook: Where do the cables go? We decide that in the workshop.
ig:
A tidy desk is mostly planning. The cable route is decided long before anything reaches your house.

Here's how we work on a fitted home office desk:

At survey, every socket, switch and data point is marked on the drawing.
In the design, we place the grommets where your monitor and laptop will actually sit.
In the workshop, grommet holes and cut-outs are bored before the carcass is assembled, so edges are clean and sealed.
On site, the desk goes in with the sockets still reachable and a single route for leads to drop out of sight.

The result is a desk you can sit at without a tangle round your ankles, and you can still unplug the printer without crawling under it.

Planning a home office this year? Comment DESK and we'll send you the link to our home office furniture.
fb:
Ever wondered why some fitted desks look so tidy? It's because the cables were planned before the furniture was made.

This short video follows how we work: sockets marked at the survey, grommet holes drilled on the boring machine in our Hanley workshop, a cable tray fitted under the worktop, and cut-outs so you can still reach your plugs once everything is in.

Nothing is hacked about on site, which is why the finish stays clean.
